subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Bible Patriarchs: Abraham
overview: Abraham is a patriarch, a father of God's people. In this sub-strand you will read the call of Abram in Genesis 12:1-5 and the change of his name in Genesis 17:1-5. You will see how he obeyed, why his name changed, and how God's blessings reach people who trust Him.

lessons.title: The call of Abraham
objectives: Recount the call of Abraham from Genesis 12:1-5.
Obey God's instructions in daily life.
Appreciate God's blessings and recite Genesis 12:3.
lessons.intro: God sometimes asks a person to leave what is familiar and go where He leads. He asked that of Abram. Abram went. That is why he is remembered as a father of faith.
lessons.notes:
A patriarch is a father who stands at the beginning of a family of faith. Abraham is one of the Bible patriarchs. His earlier name was Abram. Genesis 12:1-5 tells his call.

### What God said
The LORD told Abram to leave his country, his people and his father's household and go to the land God would show him. God promised to make him into a great nation, to bless him, and to make his name great so that he would be a blessing. God said He would bless those who blessed Abram, and that whoever cursed Abram God would curse. All peoples on earth would be blessed through him. That promise is Genesis 12:3. Recite it and thank God that His blessing was meant to spread, not to stop with one man.

### What Abram did
Abram went, as the LORD had told him. Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he set out from Harran. He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, the possessions they had gathered, and the people they had acquired in Harran. They set out for the land of Canaan and arrived there.

He did not yet see the whole nation. He obeyed the instruction he had been given. That is faith joined to obedience.

### Obeying God today
You are not asked to leave your country. You are asked to obey the instructions God has already given children: honour your parents, tell the truth, love others, and keep away from wrong. When you obey quickly, you are walking in the same direction as Abram.

### Appreciating blessing
A blessing is a good gift from God. Abram was promised a great name, a nation, and a blessing for all peoples. You can appreciate blessings in your own life: family, food, school, health, friends and the word of God. Say thank you. Do not treat gifts as if you made them yourself. Sing about Abraham the father of faith, then role-play God calling and Abram setting out.

keyWords.meaning: a father at the beginning of God's people, such as Abraham
a good gift and promise from God
God's command and invitation to Abram to go

activity.title: Retell and role-play the call
steps: Sing a song about Abraham the father of faith.
Read Genesis 12:1-5 and retell the call of Abraham.
Role-play the call: one learner speaks God's command, and another gathers the family and sets out.
Recite Genesis 12:3 and each learner names one blessing to thank God for.

practice.question: What did God tell Abram to leave?
practice.answer: His country, his people and his father's household.

practice.question: How old was Abram when he set out from Harran, and who went with him?
practice.answer: He was seventy-five. He took Sarai, his nephew Lot, their possessions and the people they had acquired. They went to Canaan.

practice.question: Recite the promise in Genesis 12:3 about all peoples.
practice.answer: All peoples on earth will be blessed through Abram.

summary: God called Abram to leave his country and go to a land God would show him.
Abram obeyed. He was seventy-five when he left Harran for Canaan.
Genesis 12:3 says all peoples on earth will be blessed through him.

lessons.title: From Abram to Abraham
objectives: Mention his or her own name and say what he or she likes about it.
Discuss why Abram's name was changed to Abraham.
lessons.intro: Names carry meaning. Your name identifies you. Abram received a new name from God because God was making him the father of many nations.
lessons.notes:
Genesis 17:1-5 tells the change of name. When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty; walk before me faithfully and be blameless." God promised to make His covenant with Abram and to increase his numbers greatly. Abram fell facedown. God said Abram would be the father of many nations. Then God said, "No longer will you be called Abram; your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations."

### Why the name changed
The verse gives the reason. The new name, Abraham, was given because God had made him a father of many nations. The change was God's act, not Abram's idea. It was tied to the covenant, God's binding promise. From this point the Bible uses the name Abraham for the man who was called in Genesis 12.

Discuss the change with a partner. Ask: Who changed the name? God. When? When Abram was ninety-nine. Why? Because he would be the father of many nations. What was he told to do? Walk before God faithfully and be blameless.

### Your own name
God knows the name you use now. Mention it with confidence. Say what you like about it. It may be the name a parent chose, a name that sounds like a grandparent's, or a name you have learnt to answer to at school. Liking your name is part of self-identity. You do not need a new name to be known by God. Abraham's new name marked a promise. Your name already marks you as the child your family calls.

If someone mocks your name, remember that names matter to God. He gave Abraham a name full of promise. Speak your name clearly and kindly correct a person who twists it.

keyWords.meaning: knowing who you are, including your name
the name God used for Himself when He appeared to Abram in Genesis 17:1

examples.problem: A classmate asks, "Why was Abram called Abraham?" Answer from Genesis 17:5 only.
steps: The verse says, "for I have made you a father of many nations."
Do not add a reason the verse does not give.
examples.answer: God changed Abram's name to Abraham because He had made him a father of many nations.

activity.title: Read the new name and talk about yours
steps: Read Genesis 17:1-5 on the change of Abraham's name.
In groups, discuss why the name Abram was changed.
Each learner says his or her name and one thing he or she likes about it.
Write the sentence: "God changed Abram to Abraham because he would be the father of many nations."

practice.question: How old was Abram when God changed his name?
Why was Abram's name changed to Abraham?
practice.answer: Because God had made him a father of many nations.

practice.question: What does it mean to mention your name for self-identity?
practice.answer: To say my name clearly and know that it identifies me.

summary: At ninety-nine, Abram was named Abraham.
God changed the name because Abraham would be the father of many nations.
Your own name is part of who you are. Say it with thanks.

quiz.question: A patriarch in this lesson is...
options: a father at the beginning of God's people
quiz.explanation: Abraham is called a Bible patriarch, a father of faith.

quiz.question: God told Abram to leave...
options: his country, his people and his father's household
Egypt and never return to Canaan

quiz.question: How old was Abram when he left Harran?
quiz.explanation: Genesis 12:4 says he was seventy-five years old.

quiz.question: Abram obeyed God by...
quiz.answer: Going as the LORD had told him, taking Sarai, Lot and their household to Canaan.

quiz.question: Which daily action follows Abraham's example of obedience?
options: Obeying God's word and rightful instructions
Refusing to go where you are sent on an errand
quiz.explanation: Abraham did what God said. Children obey God's word in daily life.

quiz.question: Genesis 12:3 says that all peoples on earth will be:
quiz.explanation: The promise is that all peoples will be blessed through him.

quiz.question: Appreciating God's blessings means...
options: thanking God for His good gifts
claiming you made every gift yourself
quiz.explanation: Genesis 12:3 is recited so learners appreciate God's blessing.

quiz.question: Why did God change the name Abram?
options: Abram asked for a shorter name
Because God made him a father of many nations

quiz.question: Abram was how old at the time of the name change?
Mentioning your name for self-identity means:
quiz.answer: Saying my name so that I know and show who I am.
quiz.explanation: The outcome links a learner's own name with Abraham's story of a name given by God.
